mechanism_narrative: The monotone four-week recovery in RETAIL_REC (from -52.7 to -30.7) and in WORKPLACES (from -30.7 to -23.9) reflects a self-sustaining reopening of commuting and discretionary trips, so the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC will be higher than the last 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rises every week from -52.7 to -30.7
fact:WORKPLACES rises every week from -30.7 to -23.9
failure_condition: The mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days while WORKPLACES keeps rising week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: Once the PARKS weekly mean crosses above -15 percent change from baseline, outdoor leisure becomes a normal routine rather than a rare exception, and the correlated discretionary trips raise RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean rises above -15 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumps from -37.3 to -14.3 then reaches -6.9
failure_condition: After PARKS crosses above -15, the following 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than the 28-day mean recorded before the crossing.
